verdict: It functions and it does not convert. Every mana axis is at or over target and the turn-3 land drop lands 90%, so nothing downstream is waiting on mana; five checker-passed stacks record what the board can do. What limits it is turning bodies into life totals — across 100 games on the standard pod it won 3 (0.031, ci95 [0.01, 0.086]) against the 0.144 seat-0 null this table gives our decks, dealt a median 4.0 combat damage against a mean 44.58 taken, and dealt a mean 0.28 noncombat damage to players (median 0, ci95 [0.01, 0.55]) while a mean 4.93 token-creation events resolved. threat-density reads 2 because the taxonomy files the ten reach cards as removal, and the ceiling assembles 26.5% because the storm target is an AND of two independent four-card groups.

open_questions.why_it_matters: If it is lethal from a wide board, Blasphemous Act is a third finisher and threat-density is answered without buying anything.

gaps: ANSWERED SINCE THE LAST DIAGNOSIS, and recorded rather than dropped: the previous document's complaint that mana_analysis credited Goblin Burrows and Kher Keep as red land sources off a colour-identity fallback is fixed. manabase.land_colors removed the fallback and names this deck in its own comment ("goblin-storm's red land count was 33 and is 31"). Glimpse the Impossible lost its red the same way, taking nonland red sources 7 -> 6. colour-sources therefore reads 1, not 4, and the drop is the defect being corrected, not the deck getting worse.

There is no deck_recon.json for this deck (deck-audit reports recon present: false), so nothing here is grounded in what other Zada or Goblin-storm lists actually run. Every add is corpus-mined, not meta-sourced.

The captain's log now has two entries (001, 002), both losses, and NEITHER is debriefed — there is no log_annotations.json. Two entries sharing a takeaway is a finding; it is still two games, and I have used them only to name a keep discipline, never to move an axis.

The strongest table evidence is a 100-game run against the standard pod (giada-angels, baylen-tokens, abaddon): 3 wins, 0.031, ci95 [0.01, 0.086], mean round 20.19, against a 0.144 seat-0 null for this table over 8 runs and 619 games. Every seat is Forge's AI, whose own docs call it "pretty bad for most combo decks" — so this deck's win rate is NOT a measurement of its ceiling. The figures I lean on — combat damage dealt and taken, noncombat damage dealt, token attackers — are structural rather than skill-bound, but the corpus also records that Forge's AI under-uses sacrifice outlets and activated abilities, so the 0.28 noncombat figure is a FLOOR on what the reach package would do in a pilot's hands.

The deck has never been simulated against a second, slower pod, so nothing here separates 'this deck is slow' from 'this table is fast'. 73 of its 75 recorded eliminations were by damage and giada-angels dealt 50 of them.

deck-audit's mana-sources axis names Impulsive Pilferer and Storm-Kiln Artist among five persistent producers, while mana_analysis.json excludes both from its producer list. Both read card_roles.json, which tags each ramp:dork as well as ramp:treasure. The two commands disagree and I have not picked one; the residual is in the roles file, not in either command.

strategic_frame.json quotes the Zada pivot at 66.1% / 49.6% / mean turn 5.27 where deck-audit now computes 66.3% / 50.1% / 5.245. The frame is prose written against an earlier goldfish; I carried the audit's figures and the frame is stale by three decimals, not wrong in substance.

bracket_report.json sets target 4 and within_target true, so the deck is inside its intended bracket by contents — but the file carries no decklist_sha256 and deck-audit's freshness block reports it as unstamped, so nothing confirms it was computed on this list.

card_roles.json classifies 87.3% of this deck; ten entries have no role at all (Chaos Warp, Crimson Wisps, Daring Discovery, Expedite, Fists of Flame, Past in Flames, Reliquary Tower, Renegade Tactics, Spreading Insurrection, Wild Ride). Several are load-bearing: grepping all 79 entries for destroy / exile / counter target / return target / gain control returns fifteen cards, of which Goblin Trashmaster and Vandalblast answer artifacts, Spreading Insurrection answers a creature, and the remainder act on your own library or graveyard — which leaves Chaos Warp, role-less, as the deck's answer to an opposing enchantment or land. Every role-derived axis here is a floor rather than a count.

The goldfish's mulligan rule is "keep 7-card hands with 2-5 lands" with no gate on Goblin presence, and its lands always enter untapped. Both are stated assumptions rather than defects, but they mean the 79.1% keep rate and the 90% turn-3 land drop are measured under a keep policy and a tapland model that are kinder than the table.
deck-facts reports 42 synergy edges falling inside this deck, but the synergy graph is a format-wide top-10 shortlist and not a fit score, so no claim in this document rests on it.

Four combo lines are contained in the deck. One — Storm-Kiln Artist + Haze of Rage — is verified by stack 005. The three Krenko lines were examined by stack 004, also checker-passed, which found they do not produce their advertised infinite here because Zada is the commander and a sacrificed Krenko stays in the graveyard.

Roaming Throne is counted as one of the two protection copies on the strength of ward {2}; its actual job is doubling a chosen creature type's triggers, and no artifact settles which type it should name or whether Zada's copy trigger is doubled.
